title: The Extent of Anomalies
description: What can an anomaly do, and how big can it get? Catalogue them, and their sizes - tumours, outbreaks, avalanches, ruptures - follow power laws: most are tiny, a few are vast, and the mean is set by the exponent. Unlocks the Anomaly Catalogue.

puzzle.goal: Catalogue anomalies by size - tumours, outbreaks, avalanches, ruptures - and above a smallest size s₀ their sizes follow a power law: the probability density falls off as s^(−τ), normalised by (τ − 1)/s₀. Write the mean size of an anomaly.
puzzle.name: mean of a power-law (Pareto) distribution
puzzle.ask: For τ > 2 the integral is s₀(τ − 1)/(τ − 2); at τ ≤ 2 it diverges - the largest anomaly dominates everything. With s₀ = s, find the mean size.

vars.s: anomaly size (s₀ in step 2: the smallest size)

puzzle.method: Substitute u = s/s₀: the integrand becomes (τ − 1)u^{1−τ}, and ∫₁^∞ u^{1−τ}du = 1/(τ − 2).
